page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.small is an entry-level virtual server instance within the shared family architecture, provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. The CPU exposes AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES instructions. The system includes 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not bundle any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, requiring workloads to rely on remote cloud storage options.

Across benchmark evaluations, the ecs.n1.small ranks in the bottom 10 percent of recorded systems. The single vCPU architecture limits both single-core and multi-core stress-ng throughput to a score of 1026.39, while the PassMark CPU test recorded an aggregate score of 1291.58. Memory subsystem benchmarks show a cached read bandwidth of 76.38 GB/sec on small 16 KB blocks, dropping to 8.4 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB reads and 6.9 GB/sec on large block writes, leading to a PassMark memory score of 673.93. Application-level metrics reflect these throughput constraints, achieving 1.35 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and a static web serving rate of 0.91 GB/sec.

Given its minimal compute footprint and lack of bundled local storage, the instance prioritizes low entry cost over raw processing capacity. The single vCPU and 2.0 GB memory envelope limit concurrency and prohibit intensive computational or memory-heavy applications. Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.small is functionally suitable for lightweight background processing, low-traffic test environments, small utility scripts, or basic monitoring agents that operate within strict resource boundaries.

In benchmark assessments, it consistently ranks within the bottom 10 percent of evaluated systems, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 1291.58, an uncached memory read bandwidth of 8.4 GB/sec, and 1.35 million Redis SET operations per second. With minimal resource density, the instance trades high throughput for cost-conscious hardware allocation. It is best applied to lightweight development, continuous integration workers, entry-level web testing, and low-throughput utility jobs.
